channel.title: VOLTFIELD Supply Co. — Insights & Guides
channel.description: Procurement guides, buying guides, and reference data for energy infrastructure and industrial MRO sourcing, from VOLTFIELD Supply Co.

item.title: Pad-Mount vs. GSU Transformers: Which Do You Need?
item.description: Pad-mount and GSU transformers solve different problems and carry different lead times (85 weeks vs. 144 weeks). How to tell which one your project actually needs.

item.title: Glossary — Energy & Industrial Equipment Terms Explained
item.description: Plain-language definitions for the standards and terms that show up across energy infrastructure and industrial procurement: ANSI C57, API 5CT/6A/7K/16A, NFPA 855, UL 9540A, FEOC, and more.

item.title: The Voltfield Lead-Time Index
item.description: Current indicative lead times and pricing across data center power, renewables, battery storage, and oilfield equipment, compiled from the same data driving the catalog's lead-time flags.

item.title: FEOC Compliance for Solar & Storage Procurement: A Practical Guide
item.description: What FEOC rules mean for solar and storage procurement, what changed with Treasury's safe-harbor guidance, and what documentation buying teams should be gathering now.

item.title: Why Transformer Lead Times Stretch Past 3 Years — And How to Plan Around It
item.description: What's driving the multi-year power transformer shortage, and practical steps procurement teams can take to protect their project timeline.

item.title: How to Read a Transformer Nameplate: A Field Guide
item.description: What every field on a power or distribution transformer nameplate actually means, and how to use them when specifying or comparing units.

item.title: Switchgear Compartment Types Explained: Metal-Clad vs. Metal-Enclosed
item.description: What separates metal-clad from metal-enclosed switchgear, what's inside each compartment of a metal-clad lineup, and why the distinction affects lead time and spec compliance.

item.title: Arc-Flash Boundary Basics: What Procurement and Facilities Teams Need to Know
item.description: What an arc-flash boundary is, how it relates to incident energy and NFPA 70E, and what documentation buying teams should expect — not a substitute for a licensed study.

item.title: BESS Fire Safety Basics: NFPA 855 & UL 9540A Explained
item.description: What NFPA 855 actually requires for battery energy storage system installations, how UL 9540A large-scale fire testing sets separation distances, and why site layout decisions need to happen before equipment is ordered.

item.title: Grounding & Bonding Basics for Industrial Electrical Systems
item.description: Grounding and bonding get used interchangeably in conversation but do two different jobs. What each one actually does, why the equipment grounding conductor matters more than the ground rod, and how separately derived systems change the rules.

item.title: Short-Circuit Studies & Breaker Coordination Basics
item.description: What a short-circuit study actually calculates, why a quick infinite-source fault-current estimate isn't a substitute for one, and how breaker coordination decides which device trips first when something goes wrong.

item.title: The Grid Interconnection Process, Explained: Queue to Interconnection Agreement
item.description: What actually happens between filing an interconnection request and energizing a generation project — queue position, feasibility/system impact/facilities studies, cluster studies, and the interconnection agreement.

item.title: Buy America / Build America, Buy America (BABA) for Infrastructure Procurement
item.description: What the Build America, Buy America Act (BABA) actually requires for IIJA-funded infrastructure projects, how it differs from the IRA domestic content bonus, and what documentation to gather.

item.title: POD & Skid Designer
item.description: A free power POD/skid sizing sandbox: set a target load and redundancy level (N/N+1/2N), pick a transformer, switchgear, distribution, backup power, and cooling, then check sizing instantly.

item.title: PJM Interconnection Timeline, Explained: Transition Cycles & Data Center Load
item.description: How PJM's interconnection queue actually works: the Transition Cycle reform that replaced serial studies, readiness requirements, and what the Northern Virginia data-center load boom means for queue timing.

item.title: MISO Interconnection Timeline, Explained: The Definitive Planning Phase
item.description: How MISO's Definitive Planning Phase (DPP) cluster-study process works, why it ran into major delays, and why a single MISO timeline doesn't apply evenly across its North, Central, and South regions.

item.title: ERCOT Interconnection Timeline, Explained: Why Texas Runs Its Own Process
item.description: How ERCOT's generation interconnection process works, why it isn't FERC-jurisdictional, and how rapid wind, solar, and storage growth has reshaped what was once one of the faster queues in the US.

item.title: Rack Elevation Builder
item.description: A free rack elevation planner: stack servers, switches, storage, UPS, and PDUs into a 24/42/48U rack and check U-space, circuit power (NEC 80% continuous-load derate), and weight budgets instantly.

item.title: PUE Explained
item.description: The formula, typical ranges from 1.1 to 2.0, what actually drives PUE down, and where the metric falls short.

item.title: Liquid Cooling vs. Air Cooling for AI-Density Racks
item.description: Direct-to-chip, immersion, and rear-door heat exchangers explained, plus retrofit vs. new-build tradeoffs.

item.title: BESS Augmentation Explained
item.description: Why battery storage capacity fades, and how augmentation plans for it with phased DC block additions.

item.title: Inverter Clipping Ratio Explained
item.description: Why utility-scale solar sites oversize the DC array on purpose, and typical DC:AC ratios by site profile.
